ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the line $y_1=k_1x+b$ intersects with the hyperbola $y_2=\frac{k_2}{x}$ at points $A(-2, 3)$ and $B(m, -2)$. What are the expressions for the functions corresponding to $y_1$ and $y_2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let point $A\left(-2, 3\right)$ be substituted into the equation of the inverse proportion function to find: $k=-6$,\\
$\therefore y_{2}=-\frac{6}{x}$,\\
$\because$ point B is on the graph of the inverse proportion function,\\
$\therefore -2m=-6$, which gives: $m=3$,\\
$\therefore B\left(3, -2\right)$,\\
Substituting points A and B into the equation of the line gives: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}
-2k_{1}+b=3 \\
3k_{1}+b=-2
\end{array}\right.$, solving this yields: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}
k_{1}=-1 \\
b=1
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore y_{1}=\boxed{-x+1}$;

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the line $y_1=k_1x+b$ intersects with the hyperbola $y_2=\frac{k_2}{x}$ at points $A(-2, 3)$ and $B(m, -2)$. What are the expressions for the functions corresponding to $y_1$ and $y_2$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Let point $A\left(-2, 3\right)$ be substituted into the equation of the inverse proportion function to find: $k=-6$,\\
$\therefore y_{2}=-\frac{6}{x}$,\\
$\because$ point B is on the graph of the inverse proportion function,\\
$\therefore -2m=-6$, which gives: $m=3$,\\
$\therefore B\left(3, -2\right)$,\\
Substituting points A and B into the equation of the line gives: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}
-2k_{1}+b=3 \\
3k_{1}+b=-2
\end{array}\right.$, solving this yields: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}
k_{1}=-1 \\
b=1
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore y_{1}=\boxed{-x+1}$;
